spec.text:
**Ozone incident lab** (Ozone 2.0.0, 3 OM + 3 SCM, lab RPC capacity 1:200).

How to read: a full OM queue alone does not mean failure. Check **completed calls/s**:
high = busy, near 0 = stuck. Then check SCM 9863 (row 2): if SCM is slow, OM handlers wait on SCM.
Row 3 follows a delete from OM to SCM. Row 4 shows if the SCM state machine keeps up.

display.name: 1, 2) rpc_call_queue_length (OM 9862 and SCM 9863 call queue (production view))
display.description: 1) OM queue climbing? 2) SCM 9863 queue climbing too?

display.name: 2) rpc_rpc_processing_time_num_ops (SCM 9863 completed calls/s)
display.description: Near 0 on the SCM leader while its queue climbs = scm1 is stuck (right side of the flowchart). Still finishing calls = OM side (3a, 3b).

display.name: 3a, 4) jvm_metrics_gc_time_millis (JVM GC time ms/s (OM and SCM))
display.description: 3a) OM lines, 4) SCM lines. Near 1000 ms/s, or gaps in the scm1 line = JVM frozen by GC. Near 0 = no.

display.name: 3b) Recon load on the OM (pull the Recon log)

spec.text:
**Not a metric here** (Recon does not run in the lab).

Production: in the Recon log, find OM snapshot / delta pulls between 06:00 and 11:00 (`grep -iE "snapshot|delta" ozone-recon*.log`). Many pulls at the same time as the climb = Recon load (C4).

display.name: 5) ratis_log_worker_syncTime (SCM Ratis log sync time p99 (s))
display.description: fsync of the SCM Ratis log. Seconds = slow disk or stuck Ratis.

display.name: 5) ratis_server_numPendingRequestInQueue (SCM Ratis pending requests)
display.description: Climbing = SCM Ratis cannot keep up.

display.name: 5b) Disk latency / iowait on scm1 (pull host metrics)

spec.text:
**Not collected in the lab.**

Production: node exporter / host dashboard for scm1, or on the host: `iostat -x 5` (look at `await` and `%util` on the SCM metadata disk). High = slow disk (C1b).

display.name: 6) RocksDB write stalls on scm1 (pull the RocksDB LOG)

spec.text:
**A log file, not a metric.** Live lab:

`docker compose exec scm1 grep -E "Cumulative stall|Interval stall|Stalls\(count\)" /data/metadata/scm.db/LOG | tail -3`

`docker compose exec scm1 grep -c -E "Stalling writes|Stopping writes" /data/metadata/scm.db/LOG`

Production: the same on scm1's `scm.db/LOG`. Stall above 0 percent, or any 'Stalling writes' = RocksDB stall (C1a).

**A log, not a metric.** Live lab:

`docker compose logs scm1 2>&1 | grep -E "Skip writing the deleted blocks|exceeds the max buffer limit"`

Production: the same grep on the scm1 log. Any line = HDDS-11633 (C2), fixed in Ozone 2.1.0.

display.name: 8) jvm_metrics_threads_waiting (JVM waiting threads)
display.description: A jump on the SCM leader while its queue climbs = 9863 handlers wait behind one stuck thread.

spec.text:
**A command, not a metric.** Live lab, 2-3 times a minute apart:

`docker compose exec scm1 bash -c 'jstack $(jps | grep -v Jps | cut -d" " -f1)' > ~/scm1-$(date +%H%M%S).txt`

`grep -A12 "IPC Server handler 0 on default port 9863" ~/scm1-*.txt`

Same line in every dump = stuck lock or deadlock (C1c); that line is the cause. Production: `jstack <scm pid>` on scm1.

display.name: lab_clock_hour (Lab clock (hour))
display.description: realtime profile: JST hour. accel profile: virtual hour (1 real minute = 1 lab hour).

display.name: lab_job_running (Jobs running (1 = running))
display.description: job01 = 01:00 bulk delete, job10 = 10:00 write burst, seed = pre-load.

display.name: lab_fault_active, lab_writer_on, lab_writer_clients (Fault active, writer on, writer clients alive)
display.description: Writer clients pile up when OM does not answer (each client = 5 threads).

display.name: rpc_call_queue_length (OM 9862 and SCM 9863 call queue (production view))
display.description: Both queues on one chart, like the production graph: OM climbs in 15-minute steps, SCM in a straight line.

display.name: rpc_call_queue_length (OM call queue length)
display.description: Calls waiting for a handler. Lab limit = 5 handlers x 10 = 50 (production 100 x 100 = 10K).

display.name: rpc_num_in_process_handler (OM busy handlers)
display.description: Handlers that are working on a call now. All busy + full queue = saturated.

display.name: rpc_rpc_processing_time_num_ops (OM completed calls/s)
display.description: Busy = high rate. Stuck = rate near 0 while the queue is full.

display.name: rpc_rpc_queue_time_avg_time, rpc_rpc_processing_time_avg_time (OM avg queue time and processing time (ms))
display.description: Queue time grows first when handlers are slow. Processing time is the time inside the handler (includes waits on SCM).

display.name: rpc_num_open_connections (OM open connections)
display.description: Open TCP connections are not requests. Compare with the queue.

display.name: lab_om_failover_log_lines_total (OM log: SCM retry / failover / not-leader lines per minute)
display.description: Counted from the OM logs by the lab scheduler (production: grep the OM log). Retries come after hdds.scmclient.rpc.timeout (15m) or a 'not leader' answer.

display.name: rpc_rpc_client_backoff, rpc_num_dropped_connections (OM client backoff and dropped connections /s)
display.description: Backoff happens when the call queue is full (backoff must be enabled).

display.name: rpc_call_queue_length (SCM 9863 call queue length)
display.description: Production climbed in a straight line to 2.4K. Straight line = arrivals at a fixed rate, almost nothing completes.

display.name: rpc_num_in_process_handler (SCM 9863 busy handlers)
display.description: Lab limit = 5.

display.name: rpc_rpc_processing_time_num_ops (SCM 9863 completed calls/s)
display.description: Only the SCM leader does real work. Followers answer 'not leader'.

display.name: rpc_rpc_queue_time_avg_time, rpc_rpc_processing_time_avg_time (SCM 9863 avg queue time and processing time (ms))
rpc_call_queue_length (SCM 9863 queue growth (calls per minute))
display.description: Slope of the queue. If SCM handlers do not finish, the OM times out after hdds.scmclient.rpc.timeout and sends the call again, so the slope = OM handlers / rpc timeout (production 100 / 15 min = 6.7/min = 400/h).

display.name: scm_block_location_protocol_counter (SCM block protocol calls/s by type)
display.description: AllocateScmBlock = writes. DeleteScmKeyBlocks = the OM KeyDeletingService sends deleted keys' blocks.

display.name: scm_block_location_protocol_time, scm_block_location_protocol_counter (SCM block protocol avg time per call by type (ms))
display.description: time / count, per type. A slow DeleteScmKeyBlocks holds a 9863 handler for that long.

spec.query: sum by (hostname, type) (rate(scm_block_location_protocol_time[1m])) / sum by (hostname, type) (rate(scm_block_location_protocol_counter[1m])) > 0

display.name: om_metrics_num_key_deletes (OM key deletes/s (user deletes))
display.description: The 01:00 job shows here.

display.name: rocksdb_om_db_deletedtable_estimate_num_keys (OM deletedTable keys (estimate))
display.description: Keys deleted by users but whose blocks are not yet handed to SCM. This is the OM-side 'pending delete' backlog.

display.name: deleting_service_metrics_num_keys_sent_for_purge, deleting_service_metrics_num_keys_purged (KeyDeletingService keys sent for purge / purged per s)
display.description: Runs every ozone.key.deleting.service.interval, at most ozone.key.deleting.limit.per.task keys per run.

display.name: deleting_service_metrics_num_sub_files_moved_to_deleted_table, deleting_service_metrics_num_dirs_purged, rocksdb_om_db_deleteddirectorytable_estimate_num_keys (FSO: DirectoryDeletingService (files moved to deletedTable /s, dirs purged /s))
display.description: An FSO directory delete is 1 key delete in om_metrics_num_key_deletes. The files move to deletedTable here, every ozone.directory.deleting.service.interval (60s).

display.name: rocksdb_scm_db_deletedblocks_estimate_num_keys (SCM deletedBlocks table (deleted block log, estimate))
display.description: Transactions written by DeleteScmKeyBlocks through SCM Ratis. Drains when datanodes confirm deletes.

display.name: scm_block_deleting_service_num_block_deletion_transaction_created, scm_block_deleting_service_num_block_deletion_transaction_sent, scm_block_deleting_service_num_block_deletion_transaction_completed (SCM block deleting service transactions/s)
display.description: created = added to the log, sent = sent to datanodes, completed = datanodes confirmed.

display.name: ratis_server_peerCommitIndex, ratis_state_machine_applyCompletedIndex (SCM Ratis apply lag (entries))
display.description: Highest commit index minus each node's applied index. Growth = the state machine cannot keep up.

display.name: ratis_log_worker_syncTime (SCM Ratis log sync time p99 (s))
display.description: fsync of the Ratis log. Slow disk = slow every SCM write.

display.name: ratis_leader_election_electionCount (Leader elections (SCM and OM))
display.description: A step = a new election. Failover retries in the OM log come with this.

display.name: om_metrics_num_key_commits, om_metrics_num_block_allocations (OM key commits and block allocations /s)
display.description: Normal write traffic. Each new block = 1 AllocateScmBlock call from OM to SCM 9863.

display.name: jvm_metrics_gc_time_millis (JVM GC time ms/s (OM and SCM))
jvm_metrics_threads_blocked (JVM blocked threads)
display.description: Many blocked threads = lock contention.

display.name: jvm_metrics_threads_waiting (JVM waiting threads)
display.description: Threads parked on a lock or a future (ReentrantLock waits show here, not as blocked). A jump on the SCM leader = handlers wait behind one stuck thread.

display.title: 0. Lab markers (when did the scheduled jobs and the fault run?)
1. OM client RPC, port 9862 (is the OM busy or stuck?)
3. Delete path: OM deletedTable -> KeyDeletingService -> SCM deleted block log
5. OM Ratis, OM write work, JVM
